test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only, and all counting is to be done from left to right).

(Left) 2 2 4 8 2 4 6 4 2 6 8 8 6 7 4 5 3 6 2 8 7 1 3 3 6 8 6 4 (Right)

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and immediately followed by an even digit?

(Note: I will be considered as a perfect square.)
solution:
Given series:

(Left) 2 2 4 8 2 4 6 4 2 6 8 8 6 7 4 5 3 6 2 8 7 1 3 3 6 8 6 4 (Right)

According to the question, such odd digits which are immediately preceded by perfect square and also immediately followed by an even digit:

Required condition: perfect square - odd - Even

(Left) 2 2 4 8 2 4 6 4 2 6 8 8 6 7 4 5 3 6 2 8 7 1 3 3 6 8 6 4 (Right)

Thus, there is no such odd digits which are immediately preceded by perfect square and also immediately followed by an even digit.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.
